claims.statement: Surya is the Hindu god of the Sun.
claims.statement_id: Surya adalah dewa matahari Hindu.
claims.quote: Surya (also known as Aditya) is the Hindu god of the Sun.

claims.statement: Aruna drives Surya’s seven-horse golden chariot.
claims.statement_id: Aruna mengemudikan kereta emas Surya yang ditarik tujuh kuda.
claims.quote: Each day he travels across the sky in his golden chariot pulled by seven horses and driven by red Aruna, a personification of Dawn.

claims.statement: Surya is regarded as a source of life.
claims.statement_id: Surya dipandang sebagai sumber kehidupan.
claims.quote: He is considered the creator of the universe and the source of all life.

claims.statement: Surya appears in the Rigveda.
claims.statement_id: Surya muncul dalam Rigveda.
claims.quote: Surya first appears in literature in the Rigveda

claims.statement: Some myths name Kasyapa and Aditi as Surya’s parents.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah menyebut Surya putra Kasyapa dan Aditi.
claims.quote: According to some myths Surya is the son of Kasyapa (a Vedic sage) and Aditi (Infinite Heavens)

claims.statement: Other myths name Dyaus or Brahma as his father.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menamai Dyaus atau Brahma sebagai ayah Surya.
claims.quote: in others he is the offspring of Dyaus (Sky), and in still others his father is Brahma

claims.statement: Surya has three children with Samjna.
claims.statement_id: Surya memiliki tiga anak bersama Samjna.
claims.quote: Surya had three offspring with Samjna (Conscience), the daughter of Visvakarma.

claims.statement: Their children are Vaivasvata, Yama, and Yami.
claims.statement_id: Anak Surya dan Samjna ialah Vaivasvata, Yama, dan Yami.
claims.quote: These were Vaivasvata (one of the 14 original men or Manu), Yama (god of the dead), and Yami (goddess of the Yamuna river).

claims.statement: Surya took stallion form to mate with Samjna.
claims.statement_id: Surya menyamar sebagai kuda jantan untuk bersatu dengan Samjna.
claims.quote: Surya was not to be so easily deprived though and disguised as a stallion mated with Samjna.

claims.statement: Surya is regarded as chief of the nine ancient planets.
claims.statement_id: Surya dipandang sebagai pemimpin sembilan benda langit kuno.
claims.quote: Surya is considered the chief of the nine planets of Vedic antiquity.

claims.statement: Surya is celebrated at Pongal.
claims.statement_id: Surya dirayakan pada festival Pongal.
claims.quote: He is celebrated during the harvest festival of Pongal in southern India and by Tamils in general.

claims.statement: Surya appears in the Gayatri mantra.
claims.statement_id: Surya muncul dalam mantra Gayatri.
claims.quote: Surya appears in the important Gayatri mantra which is recited from the Vedas as a preliminary to its study.

claims.statement: The Konarak Sun Temple is an outstanding example of temple architecture.
claims.statement_id: Kuil Konarak merupakan contoh besar arsitektur pemujaan Surya.
claims.quote: The Sun Temple at Konârak, located on the eastern shores of the Indian subcontinent, is one of the outstanding examples of temple architecture and art

claims.statement: The temple depicts a sun chariot with twelve pairs of wheels and seven horses.
claims.statement_id: Kuil itu menyerupai kereta dewa matahari dengan dua belas pasang roda dan tujuh kuda.
claims.quote: the temple represents a chariot of the Sun God, with twelve pairs of wheels drawn by seven horses evoking its movement across the heavens.

claims.statement: Surya is one of five major Smarta deities.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Smarta, Surya termasuk lima dewa utama.
claims.quote: He is traditionally one of the major five deities in the Smarta tradition

claims.statement: Troll is a collective term for humanlike beings in Nordic folklore.
claims.statement_id: Troll merupakan istilah kolektif bagi beberapa makhluk mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat Nordic.
claims.quote: Troll is a collective term for several types of human-like beings in Nordic folklore and fairy tales with roots in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: Troll appearance and character vary.
claims.statement_id: Rupa dan sifat troll bervariasi.
claims.quote: Both appearance and characteristics vary, and trolls are usually both dangerous and stupid.

claims.statement: Troll can denote giant or small beings.
claims.statement_id: Troll dapat mencakup sosok raksasa maupun makhluk kecil.
claims.quote: Trolls include colossal jotner and giants (evil giants), or small goblins, dwarfs, and other underground mythical creatures.

claims.statement: Trolls often inhabit caves, mountains, forests or the sea.
claims.statement_id: Troll sering ditempatkan di gua, pegunungan, hutan, atau laut.
claims.quote: The trolls often live in inaccessible and untouched nature, for example in caves in the mountains, or in the forests or the sea.

claims.statement: Sunlight may turn trolls to stone in a tale.
claims.statement_id: Cahaya matahari dapat mengubah troll menjadi batu dalam cerita.
claims.quote: If they didn't hide in time, the first rays of the sunlight would turn them into stone.

claims.statement: Asbjørnsen and Moe collected rural tales from 1837 to 1871.
claims.statement_id: Asbjørnsen dan Moe mengumpulkan cerita dari pedesaan pada 1837–1871.
claims.quote: Asbjørnsen and Moe collected tales from the Norwegian countryside from 1837-1871.

claims.statement: Kittelsen’s troll images drew on landscapes.
claims.statement_id: Troll karya Kittelsen dipengaruhi bentang alam.
claims.quote: Kittelsen's trolls are grotesque and creepy-beautiful, inspired by northern and eastern Norway's landscape.

claims.statement: Ibsen created Dovregubben for Peer Gynt.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh Dovregubben diciptakan Henrik Ibsen untuk Peer Gynt.
claims.quote: The most famous troll in Norway is no doubt the troll king of Dovregubben, invented by Norwegian playwright Henrik Ibsen in one of his most famous plays, Peer Gynt

claims.statement: No one description fits all trolls.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada satu deskripsi yang memuat semua jenis troll.
claims.quote: Trolls come in many shapes and sizes. No one description can fit them all.

claims.statement: The modern troll sense derives from Old Norse.
claims.statement_id: Makna modern troll yang buruk rupa dan lamban dikaitkan dengan bahasa Old Norse.
claims.quote: The word troll with its modern sense of a slow-witted and ugly beast comes from Old Norse

claims.statement: Troll can denote jötnar, mountain dwellers and ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan troll juga dipakai untuk jötnar, penghuni gunung, dan hantu.
claims.quote: The name troll is used for the jötnar themselves, mountain dwellers, ghosts, and ugly people.

claims.statement: Some tales say church bells drive trolls away.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian cerita menyebut troll terusir oleh bunyi lonceng gereja.
claims.quote: trolls can be driven away by the ringing of church bells.

claims.statement: Old Norse sources describe isolated trolls living in small families.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Old Norse menempatkan troll di tempat terpencil dan dalam keluarga kecil.
claims.quote: In Old Norse sources, beings described as trolls dwell in isolated areas of rocks, mountains, or caves, live together in small family units, and are rarely helpful to human beings.

claims.statement: Trolls may appear grotesque or humanlike.
claims.statement_id: Rupa troll dapat buruk atau menyerupai manusia.
claims.quote: Depending on the source, their appearance varies greatly; trolls may be ugly and slow-witted, or look and behave exactly like human beings

claims.statement: Folklore links some landmarks to sun-exposed trolls.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat mengaitkan beberapa bentuk alam dengan troll yang terkena matahari.
claims.quote: In Scandinavian folklore, trolls are sometimes associated with particular landmarks (sometimes said to have been formed by a troll having been exposed to sunlight).

claims.statement: Baal is a god of fertility and rain.
claims.statement_id: Baal adalah dewa kesuburan dan hujan.
claims.quote: Baal (also given as Ba'al) is a Canaanite-Phoenician god of fertility and weather, specifically rainstorms.

claims.statement: Baal was also a title meaning lord.
claims.statement_id: Nama Baal juga gelar berarti penguasa bagi sejumlah dewa.
claims.quote: The name was also used as a title, however, meaning "Lord" and was applied to a number of different deities throughout the ancient Near East.

claims.statement: Ugarit excavations revealed thousands of cuneiform tablets.
claims.statement_id: Penggalian Ugarit menemukan ribuan lempeng bertulis.
claims.quote: Excavations of the ancient city of Ugarit (modern-day Ras Shamra, Syria) beginning in 1929 CE revealed thousands of cuneiform tablets

claims.statement: Baal often refers to Baal Hadad, storm and rain god.
claims.statement_id: Baal kerap merujuk kepada Baal Hadad, dewa badai dan hujan.
claims.quote: most frequently used to refer to Baal Hadad (also Ba'al Adad), the god of storms and rain

claims.statement: Ugaritic accounts name Baal as El’s son living on Mount Zaphon.
claims.statement_id: Di Ugarit, Baal disebut putra El dan tinggal di Gunung Zaphon.
claims.quote: He is referenced as the son of El, the king of the gods, in Ugarit and is said to live in a palace on Mount Zaphon.

claims.statement: A stele shows Baal with a club and lightning bolt.
claims.statement_id: Prasasti menampilkan Baal membawa gada dan petir.
claims.quote: A stele from the site shows him with a club in one hand and a lightning bolt in the other

claims.statement: Baal’s tales involve Yamm and Mot.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Baal melibatkan Yamm, dewa laut, dan Mot, dewa kematian.
claims.quote: Yamm, god of the seas, and Mot, the god of death, were also closely associated with Baal through the stories about him

claims.statement: The earth becomes barren in Baal’s absence.
claims.statement_id: Tanah menjadi tandus ketika Baal tidak hadir.
claims.quote: As he was the god of rain and fertility, the earth becomes barren in his absence

claims.statement: Anat attacks and kills Mot.
claims.statement_id: Anat menyerang dan membunuh Mot.
claims.quote: Anat, swearing revenge, attacks and kills Mot.

claims.statement: The dying-and-returning interpretation is challenged.
claims.statement_id: Tafsir Baal sebagai dewa yang mati dan bangkit diperdebatkan.
claims.quote: this has been challenged as Baal does not actually die and return to life.

claims.statement: Baal was a warrior and storm god bringing fertility.
claims.statement_id: Baal dipandang sebagai dewa perang dan badai pembawa kesuburan.
claims.quote: In a land dependent upon life-sustaining rain, Baal was both a warrior god and the storm god who brought fertility.

claims.statement: Baal was enthroned on Mount Zaphon.
claims.statement_id: Baal bertakhta di Gunung Zaphon.
claims.quote: Baal was enthroned on Mount Zaphon, identified with Jebel Aqra

claims.statement: Baal defeats Yamm with a mace.
claims.statement_id: Baal mengalahkan Yamm dengan gada.
claims.quote: He pummels Yamm with his mace and defeats him.

claims.statement: Baal wears a horned helmet in the stele.
claims.statement_id: Baal digambarkan memakai helm bertanduk.
claims.quote: He wears a horned helmet emblematic of power and strength.

claims.statement: Baal is called rider of the clouds and linked to rain and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Baal diberi julukan penunggang awan dan terkait hujan, petir, serta kesuburan.
claims.quote: Known by epithets like "rider of the clouds" and "Victorious Baal", he was associated with rain, lightning, wind, fertility, and kingship

claims.statement: Circe is a goddess and sorceress skilled in drugs.
claims.statement_id: Circe adalah dewi dan penyihir ahli ramuan.
claims.quote: Circe (also spelt Kirké) is a powerful sorceress and goddess in Greek mythology with an exceptional talent for mixing drugs.

claims.statement: Circe is named daughter of Helios and Perseis.
claims.statement_id: Circe disebut putri Helios dan Perseis.
claims.quote: She was the daughter of the sun god Helios and the Oceanid Perseis.

claims.statement: Circe lives on Aeaea.
claims.statement_id: Circe tinggal di pulau Aeaea.
claims.quote: Circe's home was found on the wooded island of Aeaea

claims.statement: Circe turns Odysseus’ men into pigs.
claims.statement_id: Circe mengubah awak Odysseus menjadi babi.
claims.quote: Circe struck Odysseus' men with her wand, turning them into pigs.

claims.statement: Hermes gives Odysseus moly.
claims.statement_id: Hermes memberi Odysseus tanaman moly.
claims.quote: He gave Odysseus a magic herb that the gods called moly

claims.statement: Odysseus and his men stay a year after restoration.
claims.statement_id: Odysseus dan awaknya tinggal setahun bersama Circe setelah dipulihkan.
claims.quote: Odysseus and his men (who had all been transformed back into human form by Circe) stayed with Circe for a year

claims.statement: Circe directs Odysseus toward Tiresias.
claims.statement_id: Circe mengarahkan Odysseus kepada Tiresias.
claims.quote: He needed to see Tiresias, the blind prophet of Thebes who would tell Odysseus what fate awaited him in Ithaca.

claims.statement: Circe warns Odysseus about the Sirens.
claims.statement_id: Circe memperingatkan Odysseus tentang Sirens.
claims.quote: Circe informed them that they would have to sail past the island of the Sirens and gave them instructions on how to pass them safely.

claims.statement: Ovid links Circe to Scylla’s transformation.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Ovid mengaitkan Circe dengan perubahan Scylla.
claims.quote: Circe plays a crucial role in Scylla's transformation into a sea monster which is told in Ovid's Metamorphoses.

claims.statement: Circe pours poison into the water.
claims.statement_id: Circe menuang racun ke air tempat Scylla mandi.
claims.quote: Circe poured her monster-producing poisons into the water and spoke her mysterious spell out loud.

claims.statement: Sources vary on Circe and Odysseus’ children.
claims.statement_id: Jumlah dan nama anak Circe dan Odysseus bervariasi menurut sumber.
claims.quote: According to classical tradition, Circe and Odysseus' relationship resulted in three children (Telegonus, Agrius and Latinus), although some sources only mention one (Telegonus).

claims.statement: Kirke is a goddess of sorcery and transmutation.
claims.statement_id: Kirke adalah dewi sihir pengubahan wujud.
claims.quote: KIRKE (Circe) was a goddess of sorcery (pharmakeia) who was skilled in the magic of transmutation, illusion, and necromancy.

claims.statement: Kirke lives on Aiaia with nymph companions.
claims.statement_id: Kirke tinggal di Aiaia bersama para nimfa.
claims.quote: She lived on the mythical island of Aiaia (Aeaea) with her nymph companions.

claims.statement: Some accounts name Hyperion and Aerope as Circe’s parents.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sumber menamai Hyperion dan Aerope sebagai orang tua Circe.
claims.quote: Her descent is differently described by the poets, for some call her a daughter of Hyperion and Aerope

claims.statement: Circe was skilled in potions and herbs.
claims.statement_id: Circe dikenal ahli ramuan dan tanaman.
claims.quote: Circe was renowned for her vast knowledge of potions and herbs.

claims.statement: Marduk is Babylon’s patron linked to justice and healing.
claims.statement_id: Marduk ialah pelindung Babylon yang terkait keadilan dan penyembuhan.
claims.quote: Marduk was the patron god of Babylon who presided over justice, compassion, healing, regeneration, magic, and fairness

claims.statement: Marduk is depicted with a serpent dragon and spade.
claims.statement_id: Marduk digambarkan dengan naga ular dan sekop.
claims.quote: He is depicted as a human in royal robes, carrying a snake-dragon and a spade.

claims.statement: Marduk is also called Bel.
claims.statement_id: Marduk juga disebut Bel.
claims.quote: although he was commonly referred to simply as Bel (Lord).

claims.statement: Sarpanitu is named his wife and Nabu their son.
claims.statement_id: Sarpanitu disebut pasangan Marduk dan Nabu putranya.
claims.quote: Marduk's wife was the fertility goddess Sarpanitu (though in some myths his wife is Nanaya), and their son was Nabu

claims.statement: Enuma Elish tells Marduk’s rise to power.
claims.statement_id: Enuma Elish berkisah tentang kenaikan Marduk.
claims.quote: The Babylonian creation myth, Enuma Elish, tells the story of Marduk's rise to power.

claims.statement: Marduk defeats Quingu and Tiamat.
claims.statement_id: Marduk mengalahkan Quingu dan Tiamat.
claims.quote: Marduk defeats Quingu in single combat and then kills Tiamat by shooting her with an arrow that splits her in two

claims.statement: Marduk forms the heavens from Tiamat’s body.
claims.statement_id: Marduk membentuk langit dari tubuh Tiamat.
claims.quote: from her corpse, Marduk forms the heavens

claims.statement: Marduk creates humans with Enki in this account.
claims.statement_id: Marduk menciptakan manusia bersama Enki dalam kisah ini.
claims.quote: In consultation with Enki, Marduk then created human beings from the remains of the defeated gods

claims.statement: Marduk’s reign centers on Esagila.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Marduk berpusat di kuil Esagila.
claims.quote: This reign was centered, not in the heavens, but in the temple – the Esagila – in Babylon.

claims.statement: Akitu could not be held without Marduk’s statue.
claims.statement_id: Akitu tidak dapat dirayakan saat patung Marduk tiada.
claims.quote: the Akitu festival (New Year's celebration) could not be observed because the statue of Marduk had left the city.

claims.statement: Enuma Elish legitimizes Marduk’s supremacy in Babylon.
claims.statement_id: Enuma Elish mengesahkan Marduk sebagai dewa tertinggi di Babylon.
claims.quote: the Babylonian creation story Enuma Elish is a theological legitimization of the rise of Marduk as the supreme god in Babylon

claims.statement: Ea and Damkina are named Marduk’s parents.
claims.statement_id: Ea dan Damkina disebut orang tua Marduk.
claims.quote: Ea and his wife Damkina then gave birth to the hero Marduk, the tallest and mightiest of the gods.

claims.statement: Marduk seeks kingship in return for victory.
claims.statement_id: Marduk meminta janji menjadi raja dewa jika menang.
claims.quote: The young warrior god Marduk then volunteers his strength in return for a promise that, if victorious, he will become king of the gods.

claims.statement: Marduk uses Tiamat’s body in creation.
claims.statement_id: Marduk menggunakan tubuh Tiamat dalam penciptaan.
claims.quote: Marduk then uses Tiamat’s carcass for the purpose of creation.

claims.statement: Marduk was later associated with Jupiter.
claims.statement_id: Marduk kemudian dikaitkan dengan Jupiter.
claims.quote: By the 1st millennium BC, Marduk had become astrologically associated with the planet Jupiter.
